references.text: Isaiah 61:1–2 is the direct Old Testament text that Jesus reads aloud in the synagogue at Nazareth. The wording in Luke 4:18 is an almost literal quote from Isaiah 61:1 (LXX): "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to set at liberty those who are oppressed."

Isaiah 42:1 speaks of the Lord's chosen servant upon whom God has placed his Spirit – a parallel to "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me" in Luke 4:18. Jesus identifies himself as this servant of the Lord.
Isaiah 42:7 describes the servant's mission: to open blind eyes and bring prisoners out of prison, which directly reflects the mention in Luke 4:18 of sight for the blind and liberty for captives.

Isaiah 58:6 deals with breaking unjust chains and setting the oppressed free. The expression "to set at liberty those who are oppressed" (ἀποστεῖλαι τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀφέσει) in Luke 4:18 is drawn from this text, which Jesus weaves into his quote from Isaiah 61.
Isaiah 11:2 prophesies that the Spirit of the Lord will rest upon the shoot from Jesse's root – the Messiah. This forms a background for the messianic anointing mentioned in Luke 4:18.
Isaiah 35:5–6 describes the messianic time when the blind shall see and the lame shall leap – a prophecy about the miracles Jesus points to in his programmatic speech at Nazareth.
In Matthew 11:5, Jesus answers John the Baptist's question by referring to the same messianic signs as in Luke 4:18: the blind see, the lame walk, and good news is proclaimed to the poor.

Luke 7:22 is a parallel to Matthew 11:5, where Jesus again confirms his messianic identity by pointing to the fulfillment of Isaiah 61:1 – the blind see, captives are set free, and good news is proclaimed to the poor.

Acts 10:38 summarizes Jesus' ministry with the words "God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power, and he went around doing good and healing all who were under the devil's power" – a clear reference back to the anointing and mission described in Luke 4:18.
Acts 4:27 refers to Jesus as God's "holy servant whom you have anointed", confirming the messianic anointing proclaimed in Luke 4:18.

2 Corinthians 1:21–22 speaks of how God has anointed us and sealed us with his Spirit. The motif of anointing connects to Luke 4:18, where Jesus is the anointed one (Messias/Christ) equipped with the Spirit.
